title: MIWA Hotel Key Cards — Compatibility Guide
summary: Procurement-grade compatibility reference for MIWA Lock Co. hotel estates. Maps the ALV2 (Wide / Slim), ALV3M / ALV3MA and V3HTM / V3HTMA (BLE) electronic mortise lock generations, the AL5H hybrid magstripe-plus-smart-card variant, and the PiACK home-and-residential platform to the chip families they accept — MIFARE Classic 1K and 4K, MIFARE Plus, MIFARE DESFire, FeliCa IDm, MIWA's original FKL FeliCa key card, and BLE / NFC mobile credentials via the KEYMO app. Covers the 2025 Matter / PiACK HOME PG launch with SEALSQ, the Japanese-PMS integration ecosystem (Tap Co. / Temairazu / RoomKeyPMS) and explains why MIWA's FeliCa support is the genuine differentiator in APAC and Japan-specific deployments.
heroPoints: Identify the MIWA lock generation and the reader head before specifying a chip. ALV2 is MIFARE-native (Classic 1K / 4K) over ISO/IEC 14443A; ALV3M / ALV3MA add a BLE option; V3HTM / V3HTMA ship with BLE built in.

Decide on FeliCa support up front. MIWA's PiACK family and VERSA-II controller accept FeliCa IDm (Japanese transit cards), MIFARE UID, and MIWA's own FKL FeliCa key card — none of which work on western competitor locks. This is the single largest functional differentiator versus Saflok, VingCard and SALTO for Japan / APAC deployments.

Match the encoder hardware (MIWA Card Issuing System USB encoder, W105 × H65 × D40.2 mm, MIFARE 1K + 4K, optional BLE) and the back-end card-issuing software to the chip family rather than the other way around.

MIWA has no public CVE in NVD or cve.org as of May 2026 — a quotable trust signal when the wider hospitality lock category has high-profile disclosures (Saflok / Unsaflok in 2024). Combined with ANSI A156.25 Grade 1 certification and ISO 9001 / ISO 14001 manufacturing, the procurement-narrative is strong; standard validation still applies.

items: Lock model (ALV2 Wide / ALV2 Slim / ALV3M / ALV3MA / V3HTM / V3HTMA / AL5H hybrid) or a current guest card sample.
Encoder model (MIWA Card Issuing System with or without BLE option) and back-end card-issuing software version.

brief.label: Testing checklist
items: Validate opening on the actual MIWA lock generation before approving any card SKU.
Confirm encoder round-trip (issue, extend, replace, cancel) on a live PMS reservation through the MIWA card-issuing software.
If FeliCa support is in scope, validate IDm read on both MIWA FKL cards and any expected transit-card form factors.
Place the card within half an inch of the reader during validation — MIWA's stated read distance is short, and a card held too far from the antenna will not authenticate even when correctly encoded.

sections.title: MIWA lock generations — ALV2, ALV3, V3HTM, AL5H and PiACK
sections.intro: MIWA Lock Co. (美和ロック) is a Japanese manufacturer founded in 1945, ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 certified, and the largest hotel-lock manufacturer in Japan. MIWA introduced the first offline electronic hotel locking system in 1981. The current generation taxonomy follows a clear progression: ALV2 (MIFARE-native), ALV3M / ALV3MA (BLE option), V3HTM / V3HTMA (BLE built in), AL5H (magstripe + smart-card hybrid for migration estates), plus the PiACK residential / SOHO line that adds FeliCa support and 2025-vintage Matter integration.
paragraphs: A typical MIWA hotel estate runs a single generation across the room-door fleet but may have a parallel V3HTM or AL5H deployment for staff areas, service entrances or amenity zones. The card SKU that ships to the property must match the room-door reader head; FeliCa-equipped staff credentials issued for VERSA-II controllers operate as a separate credential class but can be the same physical card if the property's encoder workflow supports both.

The table below maps the most common MIWA hotel locks to their default credential set, encoder pairing, and certification context. Verify lock firmware before locking in a chip — MIWA has historically refreshed reader heads to extend chip support without a model-name change.

rows: Wide-format mortise; ANSI A156.25 Grade 1. Most common installed MIWA hotel lock outside Japan.
Slim-format mortise for hotels with narrow door rails or design constraints.
MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K; MIFARE Plus; MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3
Refreshed ALV2 line. ALV3MA = automatic dead-bolt; ALV3M = standard.
Current flagship for new hotel deployments. BLE module factory-installed rather than retrofit.
Dual-technology smart lock for hotels still running magstripe stock; "15-20 second" IR programming workflow.

Used for staff zones and back-of-house areas in Japanese hotel deployments where FeliCa transit cards double as staff credentials.

callout.label: Identification tip
callout.text: If the lock face shows the MIWA logo with a slim chrome reader window and no separate BLE module nub, it is ALV2 — MIFARE Classic-native. A small backlit indicator near the reader window usually means V3HTM or V3HTMA with built-in BLE. The PiACK family ships with a visibly different residential design and rarely appears on commercial hotel doors.

sections.title: Chip-family compatibility per generation
sections.intro: MIWA's chip support is wider than typical western hotel locks because FeliCa is a first-class credential on PiACK and VERSA-II. This section summarises which chip families drop in cleanly for which generation.
bullets: MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K (ISO/IEC 14443A, 13.56 MHz) — the historical default across ALV2 and ALV3 reader heads. MIWA's spec language references "industry standard MIFARE 14443A technology". As with every Classic deployment, Crypto-1 is publicly broken; new estates should prefer DESFire.
MIFARE Plus — supported on ALV3M / ALV3MA reader heads; useful as a Classic-compatible migration step where the encoder can issue Plus in SL1 mode.

MIFARE DESFire EV2 / EV3 — supported on ALV3M / ALV3MA and V3HTM / V3HTMA. EV3 ships in EV2/EV1 backwards-compatible default per the NXP datasheet, so EV3 stock can serve an estate originally specified for EV2.

FeliCa IDm — supported on PiACK II / III, VERSA-II, and on certain ALV2 firmware lines that expose the FeliCa antenna mode. This is uniquely MIWA — none of the dormakaba / ASSA ABLOY / SALTO platforms accept FeliCa natively. Suica, PASMO, ICOCA and other JR-issued transit IC cards can therefore be used as guest credentials in Japanese deployments.
FKL FeliCa key card — MIWA's own FeliCa-based hotel and SOHO key card. Listed in MIWA's catalog and on Amazon JP as a replacement consumable. Common pairing with PiACK and FKALT residential locks.
ISO/IEC 7811 magstripe — native only on the AL5H hybrid lock. New estates should not specify magstripe-only stock.
125 kHz proximity (HID Prox, EM4100) — not native on MIWA hotel locks. Appears only in custom integrations that pair a MIWA lock with a separate access-control reader head.

sections.title: MIWA Card Issuing System — encoder and back-end stack
sections.intro: MIWA's encoder hardware is published as the "Card Issuing System" rather than under separate Gen I / Gen II model numbers; specifications are dated 2018. The encoder is a USB desktop unit measuring W105 × H65 × D40.2 mm, writes MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K credentials, and offers an optional BLE module for KEYMO mobile-key provisioning.
bullets: MIWA Card Issuing System (USB encoder) — single SKU on MIWA's published catalog. USB to the front-desk PC. Supports MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K out of the box; BLE option enables KEYMO key provisioning to guest phones.

MIWA card-issuing software — runs on the front-desk PC, drives the encoder, and bridges to the PMS via a configurable interface. MIWA does not publish a marketed back-end product name in English; the software is referenced simply as "MIWA ALV2 Card Issuing System" in PMS-integration documentation (e.g. RoomKeyPMS).

Encoder firmware revisions over time have extended chip support from Classic 1K only to Classic 4K and Plus / DESFire. Verify encoder firmware before ordering DESFire EV3 stock for an ALV3-era property.
Guest card, staff card, emergency card and all-in-one (master) card types are issued through the same encoder workflow. Card class is set in the issuing software at encoding time.

sections.title: Mobile Access — KEYMO BLE app, Matter, partner mobile-key platforms
sections.intro: MIWA's mobile-access track has two threads: a first-party KEYMO BLE app for hotel deployments on ALV2 (BLE option) and V3HTM / V3HTMA, and a residential / SOHO smart-lock track via PiACK that picked up Matter support in 2025 through a SEALSQ partnership for the PiACK HOME PG SKU.
bullets: KEYMO — MIWA's first-party hotel mobile-key app, available for iOS (16+) and Android. Listed in the Google Play Store as `com.miwa.alv2ble`. Requires ALV2 with BLE option or V3HTM / V3HTMA hardware.

PiACK HOME PG with Matter (2025) — SEALSQ announced "Japan's first Matter-compatible smart lock" in collaboration with MIWA, using SEALSQ's PKI Root of Trust for cryptographic identity. This is a residential / SOHO product but signals MIWA's direction on credential interoperability.

OpenKey × MIWA — third-party mobile-key partnership announced in March 2018, integrating OpenKey's mobile-key platform with MIWA hotel locks for properties already on OpenKey from earlier dormakaba or VingCard relationships.
UniKey × MIWA — earlier touch-to-open smartphone partnership announced in 2014; still referenced in MIWA's catalog but largely superseded by KEYMO and OpenKey.
OpenWays — historical mobile-key integration listed on MIWA's own site; less actively promoted than KEYMO or OpenKey.
Aavgo — hotel-tech integration partner with a published MIWA pairing for digital check-in workflows.

Apple Wallet and Google Wallet — not confirmed as native MIWA support as of May 2026. Properties wanting wallet keys should confirm directly with MIWA; KEYMO and OpenKey cover the BLE mobile-key surface.

sections.title: PMS integration — Oracle OPERA, Tap Co., Temairazu, RoomKeyPMS
sections.intro: MIWA integrates with both western (Oracle OPERA, RoomKeyPMS) and Japanese (Tap Co., Temairazu) PMS platforms. The Japanese-PMS integration ecosystem is uncommon in English-language MIWA coverage and is the procurement detail most often missed by competitor pages.
bullets: Oracle OPERA — supported via the MIWA ALV2 / ALV3 card-issuing software interface; pairing common at international-brand hotels in Japan and APAC.
Tap Co., Ltd (Japanese PMS) — 39-year-old Japanese hotel PMS operator with a published MIWA integration. Common pairing in Japanese-domestic hotel chains.
Temairazu — Japanese channel manager and PMS that integrates with MIWA-equipped properties; widely deployed in Japanese ryokan and limited-service hotels.
RoomKeyPMS — published MIWA ALV2 card-issuing system interface; common pairing in independent hotels in North America and Canada that run MIWA.
Aavgo — digital check-in platform with a published MIWA integration for keyless arrival workflows.
Cloud-based PMS platforms typically bridge via the front-desk PC running the MIWA card-issuing software locally; the software brokers the PMS reservation to the USB encoder.

callout.label: PMS driver reminder
callout.text: A MIWA card sample rarely fails because of the chip itself. More often the MIWA card-issuing software version is out of sync with the PMS connector. Confirm both versions and the encoder firmware before sending a new sample batch.

sections.title: Security posture — no public CVE, ANSI A156.25 Grade 1, ISO 9001 / 14001
sections.intro: MIWA's security posture is unusually well-credentialled for a hotel-lock manufacturer of its scale. As of May 2026 there are no public CVE entries in NVD or cve.org for MIWA Lock Co. The lock hardware is ANSI A156.25 Grade 1 electronic mortise-lock certified, and MIWA's Japanese factories are ISO 9001 (quality) and ISO 14001 (environmental) certified. The 2025 PiACK HOME PG launch added a SEALSQ Root-of-Trust PKI layer for the Matter smart-home credentials track.
paragraphs: MIWA publishes a Security Statement page that documents its responsible-disclosure and security-update philosophy. There is no Saflok-style public disclosure incident in MIWA's history — the closest analogues in the hotel-lock space (Saflok / Unsaflok CVE-2024-29916, Onity HT-series 2012 Brocious disclosure, SALTO ProAccess SPACE 2019 CVE cluster) have no direct MIWA equivalent.

For card procurement: the absence of a public CVE is a favourable trust signal but not a substitute for standard validation. New estates should still standardise on MIFARE DESFire EV2 or EV3 (where the lock supports it) to retire the industry-wide Crypto-1 surface that affects MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K across every vendor.

callout.label: Procurement checklist
callout.text: Before scaling card orders on a MIWA estate in 2026: (1) confirm the lock generation supports DESFire EV2 / EV3 (ALV3M / ALV3MA, V3HTM / V3HTMA); (2) document the planned migration if any of the property still ships MIFARE Classic stock so the card programme does not extend the Crypto-1 surface indefinitely; (3) if FeliCa support is in scope for transit IC or FKL cards, validate the FeliCa antenna mode on the actual reader head before bulk orders.

sections.title: Common field failure modes
sections.intro: Field failures on MIWA estates follow a predictable pattern. Understanding where the break usually happens shortens the troubleshooting cycle and prevents unnecessary card replacements.
bullets: Card held too far from the reader. MIWA documents a short authentication distance: "place the card within half an inch of the reader and the lock will open." Wallet-thickness, lanyard wear and oblique presentation can all push the card outside the antenna's reliable range.
FeliCa-only credentials rejected on ALV2 firmware lines that do not have the FeliCa antenna mode enabled. Reader-head firmware update via MIWA service rather than a card change is the fix.
Encoder rejects DESFire EV3 stock on a Card Issuing System with older firmware. Verify the encoder firmware was upgraded to extend chip support from Classic-only to Plus / DESFire before ordering.

AL5H hybrid lock falling back to magstripe-only despite the smart-card chip being present. Check the lock's RFID-module enable flag in the locking plan — IR programming via MIWA's documented "15-20 second" workflow restores RFID-first behaviour.
MIFARE Classic sector-key mismatch after a MIWA card-issuing software reinstall. Re-export the site key from the software and re-initialise the encoder before issuing a test card.
KEYMO app fails to provision a key against a V3HTM lock. Most often the BLE option on the encoder is not installed or the property's KEYMO subscription is not yet active for the specific lock.

sections.title: Card material and thickness constraints
sections.intro: MIWA reader heads tolerate standard hotel card stock without surprises. The short read distance documented by MIWA does, however, make material and antenna geometry more sensitive than typical western locks.
bullets: Standard ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 thickness (0.76 mm ± 0.08 mm) is the safe default across ALV2, ALV3 and V3HTM reader heads.

Thicker cards (1.0–1.2 mm) — premium PVC, wood-effect, recycled-content cards — read reliably on ALV3 and V3HTM. ALV2 reader heads can be marginal at thicknesses above 0.9 mm due to the narrower antenna tolerance.
Bamboo and wood cards with a MIFARE DESFire EV2 or EV3 inlay read well on V3HTM / V3HTMA; pilot a production-thickness sample before committing to a full order, especially on slim-type ALV2 doors.
Metal-edge and anti-metal cards are not recommended for MIWA hotel locks; the shielding detunes the antenna and produces intermittent reads given MIWA's already short authentication distance.
MIWA FKL FeliCa key cards are sold under MIWA's own SKU; substitute FeliCa cards may have different antenna geometries that read at shorter ranges.
Dual-interface cards (magstripe + RFID) are required for AL5H hybrid migrations; the magstripe track format must match MIWA's documented layout for the AL5H reader head.

sections.title: What to validate before scaling
sections.intro: A MIWA pilot should exercise the chip, the reader-head firmware, the encoder firmware, the card-issuing software and the PMS connector together. Scaling before all five are proven is the most common source of pilot regret.
bullets: Test one baseline MIFARE Classic 1K card on at least one room-door lock plus, if applicable, one back-of-house V3HTM lock before approving a card SKU for the estate.
If DESFire EV3 is the target chip, confirm both the reader-head firmware and the Card Issuing System encoder firmware support DESFire before ordering bulk stock.
Run a full check-in, extend, re-encode and cancel cycle on a live PMS reservation through the MIWA card-issuing software to surface PMS-connector edge cases.

If FeliCa is in scope for the estate, validate FKL FeliCa cards and any expected transit-card IDm reads separately — FeliCa antenna behaviour is independent of MIFARE behaviour on the same reader head.
Plan a small (100–200 card) first production batch before scaling to the full property order; most field failures show up in the first 30 days of live issuance.

faq.question: How do I identify the MIWA lock generation before ordering cards?
faq.answer: Three indicators usually settle it: the visible model badge on the lock face (ALV2 Wide / Slim, ALV3M, ALV3MA, V3HTM or V3HTMA — MIWA prints these on the lock), the encoder model at the front desk (MIWA Card Issuing System with or without BLE option), and the version of the MIWA card-issuing software running on the front-desk PC. If all three are unclear, send a current guest card sample to the supplier for an inspection read before committing to a production chip.

faq.question: Can MIWA hotel locks read Japanese transit IC cards (Suica, PASMO, ICOCA) as guest credentials?
faq.answer: Only the FeliCa-equipped MIWA models. PiACK II, PiACK III, VERSA-II and certain ALV2 firmware lines accept FeliCa IDm — which is how Japanese transit cards authenticate. ALV2, ALV3 and V3HTM in their default MIFARE-only mode do not read FeliCa. Properties that want transit-card guest credentials should confirm with MIWA service that the FeliCa antenna mode is enabled on the deployed reader heads, and validate transit cards on the actual lock before scaling.

faq.question: Does MIWA have any public security disclosures or CVEs?
faq.answer: As of May 2026, the NIST National Vulnerability Database and cve.org have no public CVE entries for MIWA Lock Co. That is a favourable trust signal — particularly compared to the Saflok / Unsaflok disclosure of 2024 (CVE-2024-29916), the SALTO ProAccess SPACE 2019 CVE cluster, and the Onity HT-series 2012 Brocious disclosure. MIWA publishes a Security Statement page that documents its responsible-disclosure philosophy. Standard procurement diligence still applies — migrate any MIFARE Classic stock to DESFire EV2 / EV3 to retire the industry-wide Crypto-1 surface.

faq.question: Can I put MIFARE DESFire EV3 cards on a MIWA ALV2 estate?
faq.answer: Only after a reader-head firmware update that extends chip support beyond MIFARE Classic. ALV2 was MIFARE Classic-first; DESFire support arrived on ALV3M / ALV3MA refreshes and is standard on V3HTM / V3HTMA. Two practical paths: a MIFARE Plus SKU during the migration window (Classic-compatible in SL1 mode, AES in SL3), or a phased reader-head firmware update before switching card stock. DESFire EV3 ships in EV2/EV1 backwards-compatible default, so an EV3 stock can serve an estate originally specified for EV2.

faq.question: What is the KEYMO mobile app and which MIWA locks does it work with?
faq.answer: KEYMO is MIWA's first-party BLE mobile-key app for hotel deployments. It is available for iOS (16+) and Android (`com.miwa.alv2ble`). KEYMO requires either an ALV2 lock with the BLE option installed or an ALV3 / V3HTM lock with BLE built in. Properties that want mobile-key issuance without changing locks should specify the BLE option on the encoder and confirm KEYMO licensing with MIWA before guest rollout.

faq.question: Will premium-material cards (1.0 mm wood or bamboo) read reliably on MIWA?
faq.answer: On ALV3M / ALV3MA and V3HTM / V3HTMA, yes — these reader heads are tuned for card stacks up to roughly 1.2 mm. ALV2 reader heads can be marginal at thicknesses above 0.9 mm given MIWA's already short authentication distance. Pilot a production-thickness sample on the actual lock model before ordering a full batch.

faq.question: What PMS systems are certified on MIWA?
faq.answer: Oracle OPERA, Tap Co. (Japanese PMS), Temairazu (Japanese channel manager), RoomKeyPMS, Aavgo and a long tail of regional PMS platforms have published MIWA ALV2 / ALV3 card-issuing-system integrations. The limiting factor is usually the MIWA card-issuing software version on the front-desk PC, not the PMS itself. The Japanese-PMS coverage (Tap / Temairazu) is unusual and unique to MIWA — competitor platforms typically focus on western PMS only.

faq.question: Is the AL5H hybrid lock still a sensible procurement choice in 2026?
faq.answer: Only as a migration tool for properties still running magstripe stock. The AL5H accepts both ISO/IEC 7811 magstripe and MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K on the same lock, which lets a property transition guest issuance from magstripe to RFID without replacing every lock at once. New estates should standardise on ALV3 or V3HTM for an RFID-only path; the AL5H's 15-20 second IR programming workflow and magstripe maintenance burden make it costlier per lock over a multi-year horizon.
